messages.subject_clean: [dartR] Re: problems importing DArT object with dartRverse & loading previous workspace...
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bernd,
thank you for your feedback.
Yes that was a problem with how the Excel file was encoded!
Thank you for your suggestion.
Best,
Gabriella

Il giorno mercoledì 27 marzo 2024 alle 18:03:59 UTC+10 Bernd. Gruber ha scritto:
> Hi Gabriella,
>
> This sounds like a csv coding problem. Be aware there are 3 different csv version when you save from excel and you should not use the utf 16 coded version nor the Mac version I think.
>
> When you open the utf encoded version in a text editor you see a funny character in the first position. So this is my test to check if it is encoded correctly or not.
>
> Cheers, Bernd
> ---------
>
>
> > On 27 Mar 2024, at 18:48, Gabriella Scatà <gabry...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >
> > ﻿Hi everyone,
> > just a feedback on this issue.
> > I managed to figure out where the problem was, at least I think! :p
> >
> > The problem emerged because I used a different computer (with a different Microsoft tools packages version) to install and test dartRverse.
> > When I tried to import the DArT .csv file with the dartRverse package installed in this new computer, I got the wrong reading of SNPs, as outlined in my message above.
> > So, I tried to install a previous version of dartR in a separate library folder on the same PC, to test whether the problem of importing properly the DArT object was within the new dartRverse package.
> > I installed dartR 2.7.2, but then I had the same problem: gl.read.dart read ~59000 SNPs instead of ~ 116000.
> >
> > However, there was a warning message below:
> > "Warning message:
> > In scan(file = file, what = what, sep = sep, quote = quote, dec = dec,  :
> >     embedded nul(s) found in input"
> >
> > So, when I googled this, it turns out it may be an incompatibility issue between .csv files imported with different versions of Excel, using different encoding methods (i.e. UTF-16LE) -->
> > https://stackoverflow.com/questions/23209464/get-embedded-nuls-found-in-input-when-reading-a-csv-using-read-csv
> >
> > So, instead of reading the file that I had originally imported with the Excel version in my previous computer, I transferred in the new computer the original .csv file from DArT never opened before in my previous PC, and voila': dartR now reads 116000 SNPs - the correct number of SNPs.
> >
> > I also tested dartRverse::dartR.base, like this:
> > dartR::gl.rad.dart(filename = "C:/myDArT.csv", ind.metafile = ("C:/myMetadata.csv") # --> and it reads the correct number of SNPs too! :)
> >
> > I just wanted to let everyone know, in case by any chance you encounter the same or a similar problem!!
> >
> > And for the dartR staff - sorry to have freaked you out!  dartR.base::gl.read.dart works fine! (at least for me!)
> >
> > Thanks a lot!
> > Happy Easter
> > Gabry
> >
> >
> > Il giorno lunedì 25 marzo 2024 alle 18:20:27 UTC+10 Gabriella Scatà ha scritto:
> > > Hi everyone,
> > > sorry to be a pain, but I wanted to test some of the new dartRverse functions, following the workshop, and I already encountered some issues both in loading previous workspace (obtained with the previous version of dartR and R
> > > /RStudio 2022.07.0) and in importing DArT data with the dartRverse packages.
> > >
> > > Soecifically, I have re-installed R and RStudio (the latest versions of both) on a separate computer (from the one I normally use for the analysis) and followed the instructions to install dartRverse and the other external packages (captive, spatial, popgen and sex.linked). So, all packages required are the most up to date too.
> > >
> > > However, when I try to load the workspace I used so far with the previous version of dartR, it tells me:
> > >
> > > Error in load("~/dartRverse code/BlacktipSNP.Rdata") :
> > >
> > >   bad restore file magic number (file may be corrupted) -- no data loaded
> > >
> > > In addition: Warning messages:
> > >
> > > 1: In readChar(con, 5L, useBytes = TRUE) :
> > >
> > >   truncating string with embedded nuls
> > >
> > > 2: file ‘BlacktipSNP.Rdata’ has magic number 'X'
> > >
> > >   Use of save versions prior to 2 is deprecated
> > >
> > >
> > > Then, I tried to import the DArT object directly, like this:
> > >
> > > Blacktips2024 = gl.read.dart(
> > >
> > > filename = "C:/gabry/dartRverse code/Report_DCarcha22-7027_SNP_mapping_2.csv”,
> > >
> > > ind.metafile="C:/gabry/dartRverse code/sharks_metadata_DArT.csv")
> > >
> > >
> > > And it does seem to work and import the data, reading the correct number of individuals (428) but it reads the wrong number of SNPs 59523 instead of 116556.
> > >
> > >
> > > Have I done something wrong?
> > >
> > > When I installed the sex.linked package like this:
> > >
> > >   dartRverse_install(package = "dartR.sexlinked",
> > >
> > >                      rep = "github", branch = "dev")
> > >
> > > the system asked me if I wanted to update the required packages and I said yes without thinking so much, so I think it updated dartR.base from github. I thought this might be the problem, so I tried to re-install dartRverse from the star,t but I get the same problem.
> > >
> > > Any idea?
> > >
> > > I would appreciate any help!!
> > >
> > > Thanks a lot in advance!
> > >
> > > Best,
> > >
> > > Gabriella
> >

messages.subject: Re: ld map error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Laia,

As mentioned in the function documentation:
If SNPs are not mapped to a reference genome, the parameter ld.max.pairwise should be set as NULL (the default). In this case, the function will assign the same chromosome ("1") to all the SNPs in the dataset and assign a sequence from 1 to n loci as the position of each SNP. The function will then calculate LD for all possible SNP pair combinations.

library(dartR.base)
gl3 <- readRDS("test.rds")
ldmap <- gl.report.ld.map(gl3, ind.limit = 3,ld.max.pairwise=NULL)

Cheers,
Luis

On Wednesday, December 8, 2021 at 4:16:37 PM UTC+10 cmcdona...@gmail.com wrote:
>
> This is an outline of what Luis helped me figure out, for general consumption:
>
> *** using the current dev version of dartR (Version 2.3.3)
>
>  1. Download newhybrids from https://github.com/green-striped-gecko/dartR/tree/master/binaries. You will need to download the exe file in the ‘pc’ subfolder
>
> 2. Place newhybrids IN your working directory. The process does not work if newhybrids is in a different directory, as newhybrids is trying to look at files that are in the same folder as itself. You can either make lots of copies of newhybrids in your working folders, or change the working directory to where newhybrids is stored. Option two means your newhybrids outputs will be written to this new directory.
>
> 3. Run newhybrids via the r code :
>
> m <- gl.nhybrids(testset.gl <http://testset.gl/>, outfile='nhyb.txt',
>
>                  p0=NULL, p1=NULL,
>
>                  nhyb.directory=getwd(),
>
>                  BurnIn=100,
>
>                  sweeps=100,
>
>                  verbose=3)
>
>
>
> Things to note:
>
>  If you have spaces anywhere in your path name it won’t work. Newhybrids does not understand spaces in path names.
>
>  Sometimes firewalls will prevent the exe file running, if this happens you may have to provide permissions through the firewall program

messages.subject: error occurs after I use gl.filter.rdepth()
messages.subject_clean: error occurs after I use gl.filter.rdepth()
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I am working on a mac using Rstudio Version 2023.12.1+402 (2023.12.1+402).

First, I did start by using gl.compliance.check().  My genlight object is fine when I begin filtering and I am able to filter on maf and every other type of filter - just not if I run gl.filter.rdepth at any stage of the filtering process.  Second, I already solved my own problems by just not running this command anymore since it turned out no reads are removed at this step b/c our provider already screened on read depths.

Finally, I'm just reporting this in case anyone else has a problem. When I run gl.filter.rdepth() something happens to the genlight produced so that no additional commands can be used without failure and the same error message occuring ->

Error in array(NA, nLoc(x)) : negative length vectors are not allowed

When I first thought I had a problem I looked this up and it's supposedly often connected to Rstudio running out of memory.  I made sure that wasn't the problem.  Now I know that as long as I don't run this filter I have ZERO other issues using dartR or any other software on my genlight object.

(By the way, thank you for this amazing software that is actually easy to use even when you aren't a programmer)!

Best.

messages.subject: Re: how to restart gl.report.ld.map after it maxes out memory
messages.subject_clean: how to restart gl.report.ld.map after it maxes out memory
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

You can try:

library(dartR.base)
t1 <- platypus.gl <http://platypus.gl>
#population names
popNames(t1)
#subsetting populations
t1_pop_1_2 <- gl.keep.pop(t1,pop.list = c("SEVERN_ABOVE" ,"SEVERN_BELOW"))
#running LD report
res <- gl.report.ld.map(t1_pop_1_2)
# Saving R object
saveRDS(res,"results_ld.rds")
# reading R object
res_ld <- readRDS("results_ld.rds")

Also, note that when you close your RStudio session, the tempdir is deleted.
If you run out of the memory you can remove all the objects of your environment and reset your RStudio session.
1 Save the R objects you want to keep as shown above.
2 Menu > Session > Clear Workspace > Yes
3 Menu > Session > Restart R

Cheers,
Luis
